title: Honest Interval Length for Two-Trial Outcome-Scale Fusion with Four Calibration Observations

proof_attempt_summary: The D0 proof attempt established all-procedure finite-sample transfer, certified finite-program approximability, a globally honest fusion interval with risk below 6.05065, and a primary-only lower bound above 6.15962868, yielding a strict minimax gain above 0.10897868 for the fixed-calibration Gaussian benchmark. The decision and math panels passed after direct verification of the Folland Tonelli citation. D0.5 graded the sound result incremental below the field floor because the sharp calibrated value lacks an evaluated 0.02 primal–dual bracket and the benchmark remains narrow; a standalone reconstruction checker and the bracket remain future work.
tldr: Two randomized trials measure the same additive treatment contrast on different outcome scales, with four independent noisy observations calibrating their positive scale ratio. For the declared constant-link, no-covariate, known-variance Gaussian benchmark, fixed noisy validation survives in the local experiment. An explicit connected fusion interval has globally honest \(90\%\) coverage and maximal local expected length below \(6.05065\), while every primary-only rule, even among jointly measurable randomized confidence sets, has maximal local expected measure above \(6.15962868\). The resulting minimax gap exceeds \(0.10897868\), and all-procedure finite-sample transfer carries this gap to the limiting scaled-length decision value. Certified finite programs approximate the sharp calibrated value; its evaluated bracket of width \(0.02\) remains open.
gap: Existing scale-fusion theory compares known and unknown links through regular efficiency, while expected-size confidence-set theory supplies general duality. Neither literature determines the value of a fixed noisy link experiment under global coverage and local expected-length risk.
fill: The project proves all-procedure transfer to the calibrated Gaussian game, constructs rigorous two-sided finite approximations, and certifies a strict gain using an explicit nuisance-enveloped connected interval and an independent primary-only dual lower bound.
